applies_why: The judge treats Matthew 1:18, 25 (and Luke 1:34) as verses on a side's line counting against C3's link, which is exactly what the rule governs.
quote: [L1] Matthew 1:18 'before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost' and Matthew 1:25 'knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son' contradict C3's claim of espousal union
rule_words: a verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count
room: 'quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it ... and names that round': whether verses the judge itself marshals as links against C3 must satisfy the round-naming requirement, versus verses merely cited but unpressed; either way the judge names no round and quotes no earlier press-sentence, so they do not count
why: The judge lets these verses count against the link without quoting any earlier round's pressing sentence or naming any round, so under K-G4 they do not count as unanswered witnesses.
